code.title: Rocket Altitude Precedence Trace
code.description:
A rocketry club validates the classic height formula h = v0 * t - g / 2 * t * t with g = 10 before trusting its flight computer. Because C++ evaluates * and / before - and resolves same-precedence operators left to right, the expression g / 2 * t * t means ((g / 2) * t) * t. Read the launch speed v0 and the flight time t (integers), print every intermediate step exactly as computed, then classify the flight and print the theoretical apex height v0 * v0 / 20 as a double with two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: v0 and t.

Output Format:
v0: <v0>
t: <t>
Step 1 (v0 * t): <product>
Step 2 (t * t): <square>
Step 3 (g / 2 * t * t): <10 / 2 * t * t>
Step 4 (height): <step1 - step3>
Status: <AIRBORNE when height > 0, LAUNCH POINT when height == 0, LANDED when height < 0>
Apex height: <v0 * v0 / 20.0, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0 <= v0 <= 500, 0 <= t <= 60

mcqs.title: Preincrement Versus Postincrement
mcqs.description: Which statement correctly describes ++i compared with i++?
mcqs.Option1: ++i increments after the current value has been used
mcqs.Option2: Both always behave identically in every context
mcqs.Option3: ++i increments first and yields the new value, while i++ yields the old value before incrementing
mcqs.Option4: i++ cannot appear inside a larger expression

mcqs.title: Assignment Versus Equality
mcqs.description: Which option states the correct roles of = and == in C++?
mcqs.Option1: = compares two values while == stores a value
mcqs.Option2: == copies the right side into the left side
mcqs.Option3: = stores the right side into the left variable, while == tests whether two values are equal

mcqs.title: Double Modification Undefined Behaviour
mcqs.description: Consider the statement i = i++ + ++i; where i is a plain int. According to the C++ standard, what is the result?
mcqs.Option1: The compiler always rejects it with a compile-time error
mcqs.Option2: The result is guaranteed to be the original i plus 1
mcqs.Option3: The behaviour is undefined, because i is modified twice by evaluations that are unsequenced relative to each other
mcqs.Option4: The result is always the original i plus 2
